summary: Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Hamburg, Munich, Mainz, and under Erich Frauwallner. He served at Saarland University (~1957–1965), Mainz (1964–1965), and held the Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Mode specialized in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied in Berlin, under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at Basel. He served as professor of Oriental archaeology at Halle from 1948 to 1978.

Helen Baroni is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt. She joined the faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi around 1993.

Helen Hardacre specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard from 1992.

Helen Wang specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1998) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Her studies include training under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1979 to 1984 and held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Munich (~1961–1967) and worked as a research associate at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities from 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1936–1944) and the University of Cologne (~1944–1971).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm studied in Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught German at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair of Sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and under Paul Debes. He worked as a Referent at the Forschungsstelle für Völkerrecht und Ausländisches Öffentliches Recht from ~1953 to 1988.

Helmer Smith specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Uppsala and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Dozent at Lund (1921) and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Uppsala (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied in Berlin, Hamburg, and Bonn, where he trained under Frank-Richard Hamm, and later held a post at the University of Bonn (~1975–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated in Freiburg, Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, and Marburg, he held posts at Munich (1948–1968), the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and held positions at the University of Vienna (~1989–2007) and the Austrian Academy of Sciences' IKGA (~1988–2014), becoming director in 2007.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and Tübingen. He held positions at Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau (1955), the University of Regensburg (1966), and as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held a professorship at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, he held professorships at the University of Königsberg (1928–1944) and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the universities of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and Munich (~1968–1973), and held posts at the University of Munich (~1981–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Henepola Gunaratana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied in Sri Lanka and at American University. He served as principal of the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur (~1958–1968) and general secretary of the Washington Buddhist Vihara (1968).
